parsed.explanation: The operative regime is an enforced criminalisation framework actively deployed against trans women: the human-rights monitor documents arbitrary detention, prosecution and imprisonment of gay/bi men and trans women, forced examinations amounting to torture, and impunity for police ill-treatment; a foreign government documents arrests-for-bribes and coerced informing. This is organised, state-directed targeting (rubric tier 2, bordering tier 1 via custody torture), not a dormant statute. No protection, remedy or recourse is documented anywhere in the record; the 2023 constitution deliberately withholds protection. Ratings sit near the 0.15 anchors, slightly above only because execution is not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; entry/visa rules, document markers and screening treatment of gender-nonconforming travellers are unaddressed in the inventory.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown border practice interacts with the criminalised environment once inside; cannot be rated.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: police target trans women with arbitrary detention, prosecution and imprisonment; forced examinations amounting to torture; ill-treatment with impunity; blackmail and extortion by state and non-state actors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Criminal statute feeds directly into police targeting and custodial abuse of trans people.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facilities rules (bathrooms, wards, prisons) not documented; prison abuse of prosecuted men documented under Article 120, extending by analogy to detained trans women.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Any arrest leads into abusive custody.

care_services.exposure: Access to gender-affirming care unaddressed; national group reports rights-to-health violations for LGBT people.
care_services.interaction: Criminalised climate likely deters care-seeking; unevidenced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: Article 120 enforced (prosecutions to 2023); police intimidation, violence, exploitation of gay men and trans people 'routine'; bribes and coerced informing; constitution omits sexual orientation; proposed 'propaganda' ban; LGBTI groups cannot register.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State frames the group as criminal, licensing police exploitation and social harassment.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for travelling minors specifically; the criminalised, extortionate police environment applies to any accompanying adult whose identity is questioned.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult outed while travelling with a minor faces the same detention/extortion apparatus with added vulnerability.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: societal harassment continuing (2023); violence, blackmail and extortion from state and non-state actors with 'almost no legal protection' (2021 monitor).
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented; police are themselves perpetrators.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police abuse deters reporting, compounding street-level impunity.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No functioning remedy documented anywhere: no registration for LGBTI organisations, no anti-discrimination law, impunity for torture. LGR, facilities, care and entry rules all open questions in a hostile regime.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Open questions resolve toward risk given the documented enforcement character, per thin-data extrapolation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: morality-framework arrests of gender-nonconforming people, custodial violence, extortion, impunity, no working appeal. 0.15-C adds decoy sweeps and a latent capital clause; this dossier instead documents torture-grade forced examinations and imprisonment of trans women. Marginally less lethal but essentially the same tier.

This jurisdiction is materially worse than 0.25-B: Meridia's extortion ends in short detention, while here documented outcomes include prosecution, imprisonment, torture-level examinations and coerced informing, with the criminal statute actively enforced rather than a vagrancy lever alone.

0.35-B involves hours-long detention and release; this dossier documents full criminal prosecution and imprisonment of trans women, custodial torture and impunity — severity a full tier above, so the score must sit well below 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single national system in which an enforced criminal statute (Article 120, prosecutions through 2023) serves as the police's primary lever against trans women specifically: arbitrary detention, forced examinations constituting torture, imprisonment, bribe extraction and coerced informing, all with documented impunity and no constitutional or statutory recourse, no lawful LGBTI associational channel, and ongoing societal harassment. This is state-directed targeting at rubric tier 2 with tier-1 custodial harm, dominating every other consideration. No protection is documented at any stage of the journey. Execution is not documented, keeping the rating just above the 0.15 anchor band; thin-data open questions (entry screening, facilities, care) resolve toward risk given the enforcement character. A visitor outed faces detention, extortion or imprisonment with no remedy: 0.17.
